answer: A reputation bond turns the open ocean of new identities into a filter: each agent stakes a small, slashable deposit before joining any transaction, and the stake only unlocks after verified useful work. Like a reef that grows slowly and a ridge that breaks cheap waves, the cost of forging a thousand fake identities scales linearly with the attacker, while honest agents pay once and keep trading. Sybils drown in their own deposit costs before they can flood the market.
